chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Minqari, who said:
I heard Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever suffices himself with one verse from the Quran, from the East to the West, will be sufficed, provided he has conviction.'

key_terms.اسْتَكْفَى: To suffice oneself / to rely upon

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of relying on a single Quran verse with conviction?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the efficacy of relying on a single Quranic verse is contingent upon 'yaqin' (firm conviction), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the internal state of the believer as much as the recitation itself. This principle underscores the concept of 'kifayah' (sufficiency), where divine aid is granted not merely through ritual recitation but through a heart fully anchored in faith, a theme central to the merits of the Quran in Shia scholarship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Ahmad Al Minqary who said,

‘I heard Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) saying: ‘The one who suffices with one Verse from the Quran from the east to the west, that would suffice him, when that was with conviction’.
en.sarwar: 18. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al- Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari who has said the following: “
I heard abu Ibrahim (a.s.) saying, ‘If one considers one verse of the Holy Quran sufficient (for his protection) from East to West, it is enough [with certainty].”’
